chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Muhassin ibn Ahmad from Yunus ibn Ya'qub said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sent his hunting dog, and it caught up with the prey and had killed it. He said: 'Eat it, even if it ate from it.'

key_terms.فَأَدْرَكَهُ: and it caught up with it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat meat from game killed by a hunting dog if the dog ate some of it?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of consuming game hunted by a dog, even if the animal consumed part of the prey during the kill, provided the hunter's intent and invocation were correct. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that the dog's consumption does not render the meat impure or forbidden, distinguishing it from cases where the dog eats the majority of the meat before the hunter arrives. This ruling underscores the practical ease granted to hunters in pre-modern contexts while maintaining ritual purity standards.
